message.content:
Here’s a quick recipe you can drop straight into your HTTP client (curl, Postman, your SDK, etc.) to pull **only** the `id` and `context` fields for community comments on the domain `test4.org`, using the continuation cursor `cur456` and your API key `key123`.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments
```

> *Replace `https://api.yourservice.com` with the actual base URL of the service you’re using.*

---

## 2. Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Example | Description |
|-----------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `domain`  | ✅ | `test4.org` | The domain whose comments you want. |
| `fields`  | ✅ | `id,context` | Comma‑separated list of fields to return. Only `id` and `context` will be included in the response. |
| `cursor`  | ✅ | `cur456` | The continuation cursor you received from the previous page. |
| `limit`   | ❌ | `50` | Optional. Max number of items per page (default is usually 20–100). |
| `api_key` | ✅ | `key123` | Your personal API key for authentication. |

> **Tip:** If the service uses an `Authorization` header instead of a query parameter, put `Authorization: Bearer key123` in the header section.

---

## 3. Full Request Example (cURL)

```bash
curl -G \
  https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments \
  --data-urlencode "domain=test4.org" \
  --data-urlencode "fields=id,context" \
  --data-urlencode "cursor=cur456" \
  --data-urlencode "api_key=key123"
```

---

## 4. Expected Response

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt001",
      "context": {
        "author": "alice",
        "timestamp": "2024-10-12T08:23:45Z",
        "text": "Great post!"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt002",
      "context": {
        "author": "bob",
        "timestamp": "2024-10-12T09:10:12Z",
        "text": "I agree with Alice."
      }
    }
    // … more comments
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if there are more pages
}
```

*Only the `id` and `context` fields appear; all other comment metadata is omitted.*

---

## 5. Handling Pagination

If the response contains a `next_cursor` field, repeat the same request with `cursor=next_cursor` until the field is absent or empty. This will walk through all pages of comments.

---

## 6. Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Verify that `key123` is correct and that the key is still active. |
| **400 Bad Request** | Ensure `fields=id,context` is exactly spelled and comma‑separated. |
| **No results** | Double‑check that `test4.org` actually has community comments and that `cur456` is a valid cursor from a previous request. |
| **Rate limiting** | If you hit a 429, back off and retry after the `Retry-After` header. |

---

### Quick Summary

```text
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&fields=id,context&cursor=cur456&api_key=key123
```

That’s all you need to fetch just the IDs and context attributes for community comments on `test4.org`. Happy coding!
